summary.intent: Implement steps 16-22 of a plan for the Sessions app's Core library: adapter interface and registry, generic adapter capture/restore, window waiter, window placement, restore runner, and session capture service, with tests.
summary.outcome: All seven steps were implemented in Sessions.Core with unit tests; Release build is clean and 35/35 tests pass. The manual Notepad end-to-end restore check (step 20) was blocked by the sandbox and left for the user to run.

repo: Core uses CsWin32 (NativeMethods.txt) for Win32 APIs; new natives such as SetWindowPlacement are added there.
The spec's IAdapter { CanHandle; Capture; Restore } had no link from entry to adapter, so IAdapter.Id and Entry.AdapterId were added, mirroring the JSON 'adapter' discriminator.
AdapterRegistry forces GenericAdapter last; SelectForCapture takes the first CanHandle match and SelectForRestore resolves by id.
WindowWaiter and WindowPlacer sit behind IWindowWaiter/IWindowPlacer so GenericAdapter can be unit-tested without real windows.
Window-placement clamping (ClampToWorkArea) is a pure function, so it is unit-testable without a display.
Session name validation is case-insensitive for uniqueness among saved sessions.
Shared test fakes live in tests/Sessions.Tests/Fakes.cs.

code.finding: In a lambda that uses `_` as a parameter name, a `_ =` discard collides with it and fails to compile; the discard was removed.
A non-ASCII character accidentally entered an identifier and had to be fixed; the unused `using` was also dropped. Timeout is a named constant TimeoutSeconds = 15 with 200 ms polling.

workflow: Building Core early, before writing tests, caught Win32 signature and compile issues sooner.
Making Win32-dependent collaborators injectable via interfaces allows fake-based tests of orchestration logic.
The sandbox classifies launching and killing real processes (Notepad) as interfering with workloads, so end-to-end checks that do this need user approval or a manual run.

friction: The scratch end-to-end run that launches and kills Notepad was blocked by the sandbox, so step 20 verification could not be performed.
Compile error from the `_` lambda parameter colliding with a discard in WindowEnumerator.
A stray non-ASCII character in an identifier in WindowWaiter.cs required a fix.
open_items: Manually verify step 20: Notepad with a file reopens at the saved position and size via GenericAdapter.Restore.
The launch→wait→place Win32 path (WindowWaiter and WindowPlacer real implementations) has no unit coverage.
The IAdapter.Id and Entry.AdapterId additions go beyond the spec and are left for the user to approve.
Changes are not yet committed; seven suggested commit messages were provided.
